title: The split of RWB-E1-011 across the services and the case-side scope are not ruled by any source
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-011 sections 1, 2 and 12 (one JOB-04 step, module P1 Recovery data engine); WP B2-P3-014 story line (service rwb-case, secondary true); RWB-P1-E1011-APP section 1 and section 19 (the enterprise run and the sibling slices); FSD P3 v4 A2.5, AC-EXC-P3-027-03, AC-EXC-P3-028-01 and AC-EXC-P3-034-03; Template and Rules R3 and R6
section: s1 Story; s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s7 Acceptance criteria; s12.7 Tables owned; s19 Out of scope
description: The legacy key sits in the P1 Recovery data engine and its JOB-04 step writes one shared reconciliation_result. D-RCV-60 gives the enterprise run, reconciliation_result and the case-list publish to rwb-source-data, and the plan gives this legacy key a secondary rwb-case slice, but no source fixes where the boundary of that slice lies: which of REC-01 to REC-05 the case service runs, whether it owns any acceptance criterion of the legacy key, and whether it writes a result row at all. FSD P3 v4 applies the exclusion records of REC-01, the plan booking break of REC-03 and the referential break of REC-05 to this module, which is the only source that puts a reconciliation break in the case service; the plan gives this slice no legacy criterion and no build dependency.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-011 section 3: 'JOB-04 runs as the recovery service identity (recovery_svc)'; section 12 lists one job step writing 'reconciliation_result (REC-01 to REC-05)'; RWB-P1-E1011-APP section 1: 'This slice owns the three acceptance criteria AC5, AC6 and AC8 ... AC1 to AC4 and AC7 are owned by the sibling slices'; FSD P3 v4 AC-EXC-P3-034-03: 'the REC-03 break list for the data steward shows TRT-SYN-0702 as missing for 2 days'; WP story line: "service": "rwb-case", "secondary": true, "acs": [], "H": [] and "C": [] empty.
proposed: Rule that the rwb-case slice owns the case-side facts of the legacy key - the exclusion list of REC-01, the plan link of REC-03 and the referential check of REC-05 over the tables of rwb-case - writes no row of reconciliation_result and owns no legacy criterion, and that the platform CONs of the DP table are not build dependencies of this APP story; then record the boundary in the Change Register.

title: The case-side result row has no table and no check codes in the target
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-011 section 11 (DF-OPS-118 to DF-OPS-129 reconciliation_result) and section 13 (unique key rec_code, business_date, product_group); RWB-P1-E1011-APP section 12.7 (reconciliation_result is rwb-source-data's table); context pack ownership rows for P3 rwb-case (15 tables, none of them a reconciliation table); TSD P1 v3 reconciliation_result
section: s8 Business rules; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; s13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story writes one reconciliation_result row per check and product group, with a fixed column set and a unique key. In the target that table is rwb-source-data's, in schema rwb_source_data, with the enterprise check codes, and the ownership rows of rwb-case carry no reconciliation or quality table. The case slice therefore needs its own result, run and break tables, and no source names them, their columns, their unique key or their indexes. The check names EXCL, PLAN and KEY under the codes REC-01, REC-03 and REC-05 are equally unnamed: the codes come from the FSD but the per-service check names do not.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-011 section 11: 'DF-OPS-118 reconciliation_result.id ... DF-OPS-129 result'; section 12: 'Idempotency key: rec_code, business_date and product_group (unique)'; RWB-P1-E1011-APP section 12.7: 'reconciliation_result | rwb_source_data | P1 | Owned and written'; context pack: 'Ownership rows owned by P3 - Tables (15)' with no reconciliation table.
proposed: Create case_quality_run, case_quality_result and case_quality_break in schema rwb_case with the legacy reconciliation_result column names and a unique key on rec_code, quality_check, business_date and product_group, and publish the three check names with the story; add the tables to the service baseline migration.

title: No source names the operations, rights or response shapes of the case-side quality run
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-011 section 12 (job listing GET /admin/jobs?type=JOB-04, Power BI report, Platform administration R and Reporting R); context pack ownership rows for P3 rwb-case (22 REST operations, none of them a quality read); TSD P3 v3 API-P3-001 to API-P3-027 (no quality operation; API-P3-027 declares Platform administration C); context pack events (EV-01 to EV-05, EV-19, EV-29, none a reconciliation event)
section: s10 Authority; s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.3 Events published; s13 Solution plan; s16 Test cases
description: The legacy story answers its results through a job listing on GET /admin/jobs and a Power BI report, and its only named right is Platform administration R for the listing. In the target the results must be answered by operations of rwb-case under /api/recovery/case/v1 with a right, a scope, an error set and an element shape; no source gives them. The rerun path of AC5 has the same gap: the legacy restart is a scheduler console action and the target needs an operation with an Idempotency-Key. The rights of the two audiences differ - Platform administration R for the steward and the administrator, Reporting R for the report reader - and TSD P3 v3 declares no right for a quality read. Whether a reconciliation event should be published on rwb.case.events.v1 is also unstated, and no row of the case event catalogue carries one.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-011 section 12: 'GET /admin/jobs?type=JOB-04 | The run shows one check per reconciliation'; 'Authorization | Platform administration R for the job listing; Reporting R for the report'; TSD P3 v3 API table ends at API-P3-027 POST /admin/workflows/smoke with 'Platform administration C'; context pack REST operations: GET /admin/change-log, GET /admin/lists/{listCode}, GET /admin/parameters, GET /cases ... none is a quality or reconciliation read.
proposed: Publish the four operations of section 12.1 under the rwb-case service contract with Platform administration R, Reporting R and Platform administration U, the 400, 401, 403, 404, 409 and 503 problem set and an Idempotency-Key on the rerun, and rule that no reconciliation event is published until the catalogue allocates one; until then the run is read through the facts operation.

title: The data-product reads that replace the ACE views have no published path, element shape or product code in this story's sources
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-011 sections 3, 4 and 11 (v_ace_account, v_ace_plan, v_ace_customer, v_ace_batch_status read directly); Architecture v5 slides 8 and 29 as repeated in the context pack ('ACE data only through the owner's contract or v_ace_* views'; 'the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views (read only by rwb-source-data)'); context pack naming rules; FSD P3 v4 A2.5.3.2 (exclusion inputs, plan and account keys)
section: s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow; s11 Data; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes
description: The legacy story reads six ACE views directly, including v_ace_plan for REC-03 and v_ace_batch_status for the business date. The context pack gives the 30 views to rwb-source-data alone, so every ACE-side fact of this story must arrive through that service's contract, and DP-05 is applied as a prohibition. The paths, the query parameters, the paging and the element names of the accounts, customer and plan reads are not in the source documents, the data product codes are not given in this story's source set, and the freshness read is known only from the platform read the asset slice uses. The plan side of REC-03 is the sharpest case: the legacy check compares an approved treatment with a plan in v_ace_plan, while this service holds only recovery_case.plan_ref.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-011 section 4 step 3: 'counts the accounts in v_ace_account ... less the accounts in case_entry_exclusion'; step 5: 'REC-03 counts approved restructure treatments whose case plan is not booked in v_ace_plan after two business days'; context pack: 'ACE data only through the owner's contract or v_ace_* views'; 'Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views'.
legacy_ref: RWB-E1-011 (section 3, section 4, section 11, BR3, BR5, BR9)
proposed: Publish the freshness read and one records read per data product on /api/recovery/source-data/v1 with the product code, the business date, the paging and the element names, and build against the fake of that document; until then use the freshness path of the platform read and a product-coded records read, and read the plan side of REC-03 from the plan rows of that contract keyed by plan_ref.

title: The hand-off of the case-side hold to the case-list publish gate is not specified
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-011 sections 4 step 10 and 12 (JOB-04 sets case_list_row.publish_status to HELD or RELEASED) and AC2 ('the system sets the case list publish for 2026-11-30 to HELD'); RWB-P1-E1011-APP section 13 (CaseListPublishGate in rwb-source-data) and section 12.7 (case_list_row is P1's table); Template and Rules R5.4 and R5.5 DP-11
section: s5 Exception paths; s8 Business rules BR7; s9 State transitions; s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.2 REST operations consumed
description: The legacy step holds or releases the case list by writing case_list_row.publish_status in the shared schema. In the target that table is rwb-source-data's and the publish gate sits in that service, so the case service cannot write the status and must hand its own verdict over. No source names that hand-off: whether the gate calls the case service, reads a status operation, or consumes an event is unstated, and the status vocabulary is only implied by the legacy publish_status values. The same gap covers the exclusion count P1's REC-01 needs, which the legacy published interface excludedAccountsByProduct answered in-process.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-011 section 4 step 10: 'sets the publish status of the date to RELEASED; if any is BREAK, sets HELD'; legacy section 12: 'Map<String, Long> excludedAccountsByProduct(LocalDate businessDate)' as the P3 published interface used; RWB-P1-E1011-APP section 12.2: 'POST | the case query operation of the rwb-case contract | ... The accounts excluded at entry for the business date'.
legacy_ref: RWB-E1-011 (section 4 steps 3 and 10, AC2, BR7, BR8)
proposed: Expose GET /reconciliation/status on rwb-case with RELEASED, HELD or NOT_RUN for the business date and the unexplained exclusion count per product group, have the case-list gate of rwb-source-data read it before it releases the case list, and keep the legacy published interface as the exclusion count of that answer.

title: TSD P3 v3 declares the case links as uuid cross-references while the FSD re-base and the legacy data table use the ACE business keys
source: TSD P3 v3 table definitions (case_account DF-CAS-026 account_id, uuid, CROSS_REF; case_party DF-CAS-032 party_id, uuid, CROSS_REF; case_entry_exclusion DF-CAS-057 account_id, uuid, CROSS_REF); FSD P3 v4 changelog row for 15 November 2026 under D-RCV-35 and A1.5 ('Links to ACE records are business keys with no foreign key: recovery_case.primary_person_key, case_account.account_key, case_party.person_key, case_list_row.account_key, case_entry_exclusion.account_key'); legacy RWB-E1-011 section 11 (DF-CAS-026 account_key, DF-CAS-032 person_key, DF-CAS-057 account_key)
section: s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; s13 Solution plan (Database and migrations)
description: The technical specification gives the case link columns as uuid cross-references named account_id and party_id, while the functional specification records the D-RCV-35 re-base that makes every ACE link a varchar(255) business key with no foreign key, and the legacy story reads the same field IDs as account_key and person_key. The two readings give different column names, different physical types and different checks: a uuid reference can be validated in the database, a business key cannot. The precedence of Template and Rules R3 puts the technical specification above the functional specification, but the newer re-base and the 19-service no-foreign-key rule point the other way, so the conflict needs a ruling before the migration is written.
evidence: TSD P3 v3: '| DF-CAS-026 | account_id | CROSS_REF | uuid | Yes | None | Workbench |'; FSD P3 v4 revision row: 'Links to ACE records are business keys with no foreign key (Appendix B): recovery_case.primary_person_key, case_account.account_key, case_party.person_key ... case_entry_exclusion.account_key'; legacy RWB-E1-011 section 11: 'DF-CAS-057 | case_entry_exclusion | account_key | Read'.
proposed: Keep the field IDs and rule that the link columns are the ACE business keys account_key and person_key as varchar, per the FSD re-base under D-RCV-35 and the legacy data table, and record the uuid form of TSD P3 v3 as the pre-re-base artefact in the Change Register.

title: The report, the Schedule cadence, the alert groups and the feature flag of the case-side run have no source
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-011 sections 3, 4 step 12 and 15 (Power BI report at 07:30 on two lake extracts), section 13 (feature flag rwb.p1.reconciliation) and section 14 (alert recipient groups as configuration); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-10 and DP-17; Architecture v5 slides 8 and 37 as repeated in the context pack ('No data lake. rwb-reporting builds its read model from events')
section: s3 Preconditions; s12.6 Schedules; s13 Solution plan (Configuration, Feature switch, Done when); s15 Screens and states
description: The legacy story reports through a Power BI data set refreshed at 07:30 from two lake extracts, and it reads its Schedule, its alert recipient groups and its feature flag as configuration without naming a value. DP-17 removes the lake, the extracts and the report, so the case-side facts must reach a reader another way, and no source names which rwb-reporting dashboard or operation carries the case-side result. No source gives the cron of a case-side quality Schedule, the alert groups beyond the three roles of MSG-P1-012, or a flag name in the target form.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-011 section 4 step 12: 'Power BI: the 07:30 refresh shows each product as green, red or not run'; section 13: 'Feature flag. rwb.p1.reconciliation'; section 3: 'scheduled its refresh at 07:30' on 'the lake extracts'; context pack: 'No data lake. rwb-reporting builds its read model from events.'
proposed: Serve the facts through the read operations of this service and let rwb-reporting read them for the report of the date, register one Schedule with SKIP overlap and a catch-up window whose cron is set at deployment, keep the three legacy alert groups as configuration, and name the flag rwb.p3.case-quality-run.
